newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Gorilla survives gunbattle in S.African zoo.
newsitem.headline: Gorilla survives gunbattle in S.African zoo.

text.p: Max the gorilla became South Africa's latest crime victim on Friday when he was shot by a terrified robber on the run.
The man, fleeing from police, scaled a moat and jumped into Max's enclosure at Johannesburg zoo.
When Max tried to defend his turf and his partner Lisa, the robber fired two shots at him, lodging one bullet in his shoulder while the second went right through his neck.
The 26-year-old ape also vented his anger on two policemen who tried to snag the robber, biting one on the buttocks and arm and hitting the other.
The 190 kg (418 pound) gorilla was rushed off for X-rays at one of the city's top private hospitals, which declared him fit to return to his grassy open-air home at the zoo to recuperate.

"He's stable now. He's going to be fine," veterinary surgeon John Larsen said, adding that doctors had decided to leave the bullet in Max's shoulder, since it would traumatise him even more to undergo surgery.
Zoo officials loaded him onto a truck serving as an animal ambulance and Max went back to the zoo, his huge paw engulfing the vet's hand he was holding.
"It's just terrible," said zoo spokeswoman Jacqui Thompson. "Our reaction is shock, disbelief, horror, anger."
The robber, whom police shot in the hip, and his two pursuers were being treated in hospital.
